query: A factory owner released toxic chemical waste into the river, killing fish and affecting villagers
gold_answer: Fouling source of water (IPC 277), making atmosphere noxious (IPC 278), and negligent handling of poisonous substance (IPC 284).

query: A political leader made a speech calling for violence against a minority community
gold_answer: Promoting enmity between groups (IPC 153A, 3 years), statements creating disharmony (IPC 505), and membership/support of unlawful association (UAPA 13 if applicable).

query: A rickshaw puller was beaten by a local goon who extracted money regularly
gold_answer: Extortion (IPC 383/384, up to 3 years) and extortion by putting person in fear of death or grievous hurt (IPC 386, up to 10 years).

query: An employee stole money from the company cash box over several months
gold_answer: Theft by clerk or servant (IPC 381, up to 7 years) and criminal breach of trust by clerk or servant (IPC 408, up to 7 years).

query: A person forged their caste certificate to get government reservation benefits
gold_answer: Forgery for cheating (IPC 468, 7 years), use of forged document (IPC 471), and cheating (IPC 420). The certificate itself can be cancelled.

query: An SHO registered a false FIR against an innocent person at the behest of a politician
gold_answer: Filing a false charge (IPC 211, up to 7 years if offence is capital) and public servant disobeying direction of law (IPC 166).

query: An officer of a government department demanded a bribe to pass a contractor's bill
gold_answer: Taking gratification other than legal remuneration (PCA 7) and criminal misconduct (PCA 13) — both cognizable, minimum 3 years.

query: A girl was forced into marriage at 17 years of age. Is this legal?
gold_answer: Child marriage is an offence. POCSO Section 3/4 applies if consummated; IPC 493 covers cohabitation by deception. The marriage is voidable at her option.

query: A private company is storing Aadhaar-linked data without consent. Is this an offence?
gold_answer: Failure to protect sensitive personal data (ITA 43A, compensation liability) and disclosure without consent (ITA 72A, imprisonment up to 3 years).

query: A man wrote a will leaving all property to his son, but he was of unsound mind when writing it
gold_answer: A person of unsound mind cannot enter into a valid contract or execute a will under ICA Sections 11 and 12 — the will is void.

query: Two companies formed a cartel and fixed prices for essential medicines. Is this legal?
gold_answer: Agreement in restraint of trade (ICA 23) is void. Competition Commission of India jurisdiction also applies under the Competition Act (not indexed in this system).

query: A landlord wants to evict a tenant who has been living for 15 years and has no written agreement
gold_answer: Tenant rights under TPA Section 108 (duties of lessor). Long-term tenant without written agreement may have month-to-month tenancy; notice required. SRA 6 protects against forcible dispossession.

query: My business partner promised to sell me his share of property but now refuses. Can I force him?
gold_answer: Specific performance of a contract to transfer property may be enforced under Specific Relief Act Section 10.

query: A tribal farmer's land was forcibly acquired by a private mining company with support from local officials
gold_answer: Atrocity under SCST Act Section 3 (wrongful occupation of tribal land); criminal trespass (IPC 447); compulsory acquisition requires just compensation under Article 300A of Constitution.

query: What is the limitation period for filing a suit to recover money?
gold_answer: A suit for money recovery must be filed within 3 years from the date the money becomes due (Limitation Act, Article 18 / Section 3).

query: A soldier tortured a civilian in a conflict area. Is the army officer protected from prosecution?
gold_answer: No blanket immunity for rights violations (Articles 20-21 of Constitution). UAPA Section 49 provides some protection for acts in good faith under the Act.

query: What documents are considered as primary evidence under Indian evidence law?
gold_answer: Primary evidence is the document itself (IEA 62). Secondary evidence (copies) is admissible in specific circumstances under IEA 64 / BSA equivalent.
